evidence:
Strengths: almost every criterion names a concrete browser outcome with durable readback and positive controls. Examples: hro_restart re-reads seeded Platform Engineer order and Noor's note after restart_app (seed matches: APP-105/106/108 Applied 1-3, APP-103/104 Screen, note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.'); hro_unread_counts' Lena=1 probe matches seed (APP-301 has 3 messages, USR-CAN3 read_count 2) and other dimensions are told not to touch Lena (polish prompt.md 'Never use Lena Fischer's conversation', render gate opens no conversation). hro_refused_put_back reads document.activeElement; hro_pol_earlier_place uses getBoundingClientRect().top; hro_anonymous requires 401 plus no data plus nothing changed; hro_stale_refused requires F's readback and the changer's identity; board protocols use suffixed own jobs/cards (distinctive and not pre-seeded). Gate criteria require a UI write plus independent-context readback. Visual rows are likert with described anchors and named surfaces (shipped-format convention per SKILL known false positives) -> acceptable.

Defect (non-distinctive negative probes for role enforcement): functional prompt.md:17 neutralises only one confound - 'first read the target cards' current state and version ... and send that current value, so that only the rule or role under test can cause a refusal. A refusal that only reports the card as changed or out of date does not count'. It does not address the other confounds an IDENTICAL replay creates. Criteria explicitly ask for identical replays: functional judge.toml:173 hro_observer_readonly 'replays in the Observer's session of an observed move, add-candidate, open-job and note request are each refused with nothing changed; Rafael's identical successful requests are the control'; judge.toml:182 hro_candidate_no_staff 'Rafael's identical move, add-candidate, open-job and note requests succeed ... then replays in the candidate's session of those observed requests are each refused'; judge.toml:155 hro_mgr_early_refused includes 'opening a job or adding a candidate' via prompt.md:37 'replay Rafael's observed requests if not offered'; judge.toml:164 hro_mgr_other_job move replay. An identical add-candidate replay re-sends an email already on that job, which the rules require to be refused anyway (hireops_rules.md:32-33; golden index.js:224 returns 409 'This person has already applied to this job.'). An identical move replay re-sends a move whose card is already in the target stage, which can be refused as an invalid transition. These refusals are caused by the duplicate/stage rule, not by the role under test, yet the criteria accept any 'refused with nothing changed'. So those legs leave no role-specific trace and are not decidable for the property they claim to grade. hro_anonymous is not affected because it demands status 401.
counterexample: Plausible broken app passing: the server applies role checks to moves, jobs and notes but forgets the role guard on POST add-candidate (any signed-in user may add), while correctly enforcing case-insensitive duplicate emails. Per protocol R/N the judge replays Rafael's observed add-candidate request unchanged in Aud's, Tomas's and Ingrid's sessions; each returns 409 'already applied', no card is created, and the judge credits the add-candidate leg of hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff and hro_mgr_early_refused although an Observer/candidate/other-role add with a fresh email would have succeeded. Analogously, an app missing the role check on moves but refusing a same-stage move would pass the Observer/candidate/Bill identical move replays if the judge replays a move whose card already sits in the target stage.
suggested_fix: In functional prompt.md's replay paragraph (and the three role rows), require every role-test replay to be a request that would succeed for Rafael at that moment: change the candidate name/email to a fresh unique value for add-candidate, use a fresh title for open-job, and replay a move that is valid from the card's current stage with its current version; state that a refusal citing a duplicate, a stage rule or staleness does not count as the role's refusal.
